name: Translations
description: Plays the game in another language. Choose a language for each game in Tools > Translations... (or make your own there: the patcher writes a file with every English line of the game, its menus, events, tips, tech names and the patcher's own windows, and a built-in editor shows each line in the game's font). The game uses the chosen language from its next start, with no re-patching; lines a translation leaves out, or gets wrong, stay English. Gender and plural words follow the villager or the number (for example il / elle, 1 pomme / 2 pommes). **On by default, and English until you choose a language: with English chosen the game is exactly as without this patch.** **Letters beyond plain English (accents, Turkish ğ ş ı, Greek, Cyrillic, Chinese, Japanese, Cuneiform, emoji) need "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts" or "Use Unicode Font"; without either, the game's own font draws only plain English letters and the rest show as "?".** **With one of those two rows a translated line never runs off the screen (it is cut with "…" at the window's edge, though it may run past its own box); without them the game draws it as it is.** **Words painted into pictures (buttons, the title screen, help pages) stay English.** **Every patch's own text is translated too: its windows and messages, Custom Island Event popups, Cause of Death words and epitaphs, Son/Daughter, and the text the exe patches write; log files stay English.** **Works the same with every other patch and in every population mode.** **Not yet seen in a running game.** The companion is "VVFP Translations.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if it cannot be loaded, or the game's text is not the version a translation was made from, those lines stay English.
behavior_changes: At game start the companion reads "Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Files\Translation\Translation.txt" (written by the patcher's Translations window; docs/translation-file-format.md). With no such file it returns at once and writes nothing.

Each translated line replaces the English where the game looks it up: the string table at 0x4D31F0: each translated entry's loaded-text pointer (+0xC), after the loader; the visible literals outside the table by the address their loading instruction pushes (data/translations/vv5_strings.json).  A line is used only when the English it was made from is the English this game shows (the key's SHA-256), its placeholders match and its selects are well formed.

The patcher's own windows (Origins, Story / Cheat Upgrades, Custom Island Event) are translated as they open (a WH_CALLWNDPROCRET hook on the game's own thread, only when the file translates any of them); a message put together from several lines is translated line by line.

The companions that build a text the game shows (Cause of Death's words and epitaphs, Story / Cheat Upgrades' island event lines and Time Skip notice, Show Parents' Son / Daughter, Storytelling, Both Factions) ask for it by its line's key (VvfpTranslateKey / VvfpTranslateKeyText, native/shared/vvfp_translate.h): the translation is used only when the English is the line's and it fits the companion's own buffer, else the English.

Text an exe patch wrote ("patch/0x<va>" lines, data/translations/exe_patch_strings.json) is written over in place when the translation fits the English's own bytes (through the same all-or-none writer, after checking the live text is the line's English); a longer one is left English there.

Without "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts" or "Use Unicode Font (overrides in-game fonts)" (their companion's VvfpGlyphsUtf8; Use Unicode Font's, which starts later, is loaded and started on first use), translations are given to the game in Windows-1252, '?' for what it cannot write.
explicit_non_changes: This row changes no executable bytes: the companion checks each site's stock bytes and writes them at run time through the shared all-or-none writer, and writes only the ones the chosen file needs; if any check fails it writes nothing, not even a table pointer, and the game stays English.
No save, record or game file is written; the game's own English text stays in memory unchanged.
With English chosen (no Translation.txt), nothing at all is written.
